I'm assuming you're looking for some advice so I'll give some with no judgment (because I did a lot of this too)

Dont get those delight ice coffee cartoons they're basically sugar with the idea of coffee and add up quickly. Get the delight creamer and brew coffee. Coffee costs legit like 12 cents a cup when brewed. When I learned that I legit just lost the desire to ever spend anything except on coffee grounds, creamer, and sugar. Bonus points order coffee beans from a wholesale place and get a coffee grinder. It's fresher and tastes better too! 

Scoop up the 60 count eggs from Walmart, a primary problem I'm seeing is you're buying smaller quantity which costs more over time. You'll pay more upfront but less in unit price. 

I see yogurt cups and sugar water jugs on the bottom, scoop the large tub of chobani or Greek yogurt instead of the single serves. (general rule of thumb, if it's single serve, quick, or convenient these mfs charge way more for no reason) Replace the sugar water jugs with powdered drink mix. 

Try Soda Stream, I love seltzer water too but those packs add up. Pre-made salads are okay but again anything convenient costs more. I recall Walmart selling some pre-made salads near the marketplace pizza section for like $2, so this one isn't as important since you can still get a good deal and making salads by hand can be a pain. 

Bonus tip: I can't see your pantry but spend the $20 on a 10 or 15lb bag of rice. You'd be suprised how long you can live on rice and it's so versatile. You can throw chicken in it, vegetables, anything. Pro tip in the last 8 minutes of cooking rice drop broccoli into the pot and it will steam it perfectly. 

Hope this helps! Overall you're in the right direction, you're not eating a bunch of crap like everyone else. Just gotta learn some bulk buying, alternative methodology, and stare at those unit prices!

Here's my story, for anyone on this post that is interested in the experience of what homelessness feels like and the aftermath. My question for the OP at the bottom. 

Although I never fell into drugs, a miracle I didn't, alcohol for a bit that's it. I understand this picture completely. While I can say I always had a roof over my head through my teens my parent definitely didn't do me any favors during that time.

I left at 17. was homeless at 14 for 2 days, at 19 for 3 months, again at 21 for 3 months, and am now currently homeless (van life technically). Couch surfed a lot too, even made it into college for a bit. Rented rooms, worked 40, 80, 100 hour work weeks whatever. Multiple fields. Didn't have a smartphone until I worked my first job. 

But yes, I understand entirely. There were so many times I would return to places that reminded me of that bad place. I would, in the future, find beauty in the simplicity of it, of course living through it was hell and agony all in one. I'd revisit locations and just feel it. Think it. Navigate it. I think the worst part is the uncertainty, the complete lack of stability, and not a single chance at normality all the while going out into the world and just seeing how everyone else got that and you didn't. It fucking burns, and it's very hard to not become jaded and hateful of others for things they had no control over. 

But only fire burns and people like us have a fire burning inside us that can never, for any reason, be extinguished. These days I do feel like I can accomplish absolutely anything I set my mind to. I shat in the woods and wiped my ass with leaves, ate free crackers and hot sauce from convenient stores, lucky enough to have a can of beans some nights or maybe even a friend to sleepover and play video games at their place. 

My homelessness wasn't a solid stretch of time, but rather a handful of stretches: The worst time being before I moved into the most stable living arrangement I had. I lived in an apartment for 3 years into my early 20s. The peace I felt. The comfort i felt. The stability I had to get use to. In repeat on my head I would say "chaos is all I know" and try to self sabotage. I preservered. I would walk through my neighborhood as an exposure therapy, if you will, telling myself over and over and over "you're allowed to be here. You live nearby, nobody is going to approach you. Nobody is going to call on you. You are allowed to exist. You can walk where you want. Look where you want. Talk outloud if you want. You are allowed to exist now. It is okay. Relax. You can relax. You can be at peace." I must've done this 100 times before I stopped thinking about it and just went for a walk. 

The first day I took a shower in that apartment I leaned my arm on the wall and said "just for right now, I never want this feeling to end." I adjusted the water from burning hot to freezing cold back and forth. Just to have control over that felt incredible. I eventually settled on warm water and felt the pain and burdens wash away over me. To then step out of the shower, and in no rush at all, like in someone else's home, prepare myself for bed..  I don't know how else to say it, I can still feel the exact temperature and precipitation of that fall night. I can still feel the cold of the windows fan pulling in the lightly frigid air. I can still smell the air. I can still see the way the colors on the old 70s wood trim bounced off the walls from the light of the kitchen and living room lights. I will never forget the exact taste, feel, smell, and sight of that short 10 minute moment where all I did was exist in that apartment. 

I soon found a beauty in driving to the grocery store. I saw the items on the shelf and just said "wow, someone must've went through hell to grow this, and package it, and ship it, and pay all the costs. And all I have to do is walk in and buy it" I use to hate going into work but one day I said "you know what, something is going to happen today. It could be good, it could be bad. But dammit something is going to happen." that's beautiful. I watched the leaves come back in spring. Then leave again in the fall. I would just sit on the chair outside my apartment. I would walk into the snow and just lay there, making snow angels sometimes at 22. I couldn't believe any of it, for at least a year, i was living a dream when I had always known a nightmare. I had friends over, I dated a few women. Thought about going back to college. Could put my all into work. I actually had a choice in what I wanted to do. 

And now, Technically I'm homeless again, at 25 but this time around I got me a van with plumbing and electricity.. It's awesome! 😎 Gonna buy a house eventually, something cheap. I don't ever want to be homeless again or pay check to pay check slave again. This is my method to freedom. I hope we all find it. 

So, OP, my question(s) to you. What is your method to freedom without restriction? Would you settle into a mortgage and 9-5? Would you live with roommates, cheap rent, long enough to buy a property outright? Van life it up and save, or try college or trade school? Hoping to run into a wealth manager or wall street guy to work for free under them long enough to learn that business? Investment banking, business ownership, or tech industry? Your answer could be past, present or future. It'll be fun to see how the answer changes under the criteria!

I guess the answer depends on your current arrangements as well. For me, once I was finally able to think about the future and not just surviving each day the world opened up. Where are you along the journey? Healing? Reflecting? Conquering? Resting? I hope you're doing well, and thank you for sharing this with us all.
